sections.title: Hallelujah, the Lamb, and the rider

blocks.text: Revelation 19 joins heavenly praise over the judgment of the great harlot with the announcement of the Lamb's marriage supper. The chapter warns John not to worship the angel, then depicts heaven opened and a rider called Faithful and True, the Word of God, and King of Kings and Lord of Lords. The beast and false prophet are taken, while the gathered forces of the earth are defeated in the chapter's highly symbolic battle scene.

The chapter's praise declares that God's judgments are true and righteous. The supplied context places divine justice within covenant life, temple worship, kingship, wisdom, and prophetic critique. Revelation therefore uses royal and judicial language to present the heavenly celebration and the rider's judgment as claims about the moral rule of God.

Righteousness, justice, and divine justice are themes that Scripture develops across its story from Israel's witness into the New Testament. Revelation 19 brings those themes together in its descriptions of God's judgments, the rider who judges and makes war in righteousness, and the defeat of powers opposed to him.

Revelation repeatedly reworks Israel's Scriptures, especially Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Exodus, Zechariah, Genesis, and Psalms. Chapter 19's throne praise, marriage imagery, royal rider, sword, and judgment scene belong to that continuing recomposition of scriptural images within Revelation's own sequence.
